problem_statement: fiduswriter Simple-DataTables ships a vanilla-JavaScript data table library with a static documentation/demo site under docs/, rebranded here into DataForge, a lightweight data-table toolkit (turn a plain HTML table into a paginated, searchable, sortable data table with no framework and no build step). The docs site already ships one coherent product design system: a shared masthead <header> nav that lists the site's sections (Documentation, Demos, Learning Path, GitHub) where every rendered nav anchor carries a shared nav-link class, a shared card pattern (a .card block with an eyebrow/number label, an h3 title, a short description and a small call-to-action) and a shared <footer> credit, rendered consistently on the Home page (docs/index.html) and the Learning Path page. The Learning Path is a guided onboarding route through the docs bundle (install, configure, shape columns, wire events, load data, validate); newcomers want to jump straight to the part of the journey they care about. Add the docs site's own on-page track filter to the Learning Path guided route: a row of track tabs (All / Setup / Build / Connect / Data / Ship) above the six shared step cards, plus a live result readout 'Showing N of 6 steps · <Track>', where each step card carries a data-track derived from the doc page it teaches. Clicking a track tab must actually filter the visible step cards to that track AND update the readout to match the cards shown (e.g. clicking Data shows 'Showing 1 of 6 steps · Data'). Surface the same track-filter control as a compact rail on the Home page so the guided-route feature is continuous across pages, and keep the 'Learning Path' entry registered in the shared nav so the nav-link appears in the section nav on every page. Build the whole thing from the shared masthead nav, footer chrome and .card pattern; keep it free of horizontal overflow on desktop and 390px mobile; the active track tab must stay legible and the step cards must keep stable, non-overlapping dimensions; and do not diverge into an off-system one-off page.
required_content: The Learning Path page at docs/learning-path/ presents at least six grounded, ordered learning steps (linking to real docs pages and demos) built from the shared masthead nav, footer chrome and shared .card pattern — a number label, an h3 step title, a description and a CTA per step.
Add the docs site's own on-page track filter above the six step cards: a track-tab row (All / Setup / Build / Connect / Data / Ship) plus a live readout 'Showing N of 6 steps · <Track>'.
Clicking a track tab filters the visible step cards to that track AND updates the readout so it matches the cards shown (e.g. clicking Data yields 'Showing 1 of 6 steps · Data').

Surface the same track-filter control as a compact rail on the Home page so the guided-route feature is continuous across pages, and register 'Learning Path' in the shared nav so the nav-link renders consistently on the Home page and the Learning Path page.

Keep the Learning Path page, the Home overview and the shared chrome free of horizontal overflow on desktop and at 390px mobile; the active track tab must stay legible and the step cards must keep stable, non-overlapping dimensions; keep the existing Home overview intact.
design_constraints: Build the Learning Path page and its track filter from the shared masthead nav and footer chrome and the shared .card pattern, not a standalone page with bespoke inline markup.
The track filter is the docs site's own on-page section-nav/filter feature: a track-tab row over the six shared step cards with a live count readout — not a bolted-on decorative widget.

The active track tab must have legible contrast and the step-card grid must wrap cleanly with stable, non-overlapping card dimensions, consistent spacing and typography scale, and the same visual card layout treatment as the existing shared cards; keep the design responsive on mobile.
Reuse the shared favicon.svg icon and the DataForge card image/style tokens so the track-filter panel and step cards stay on-brand rather than introducing new imagery or off-system styling.
Register 'Learning Path' in the shared nav and surface the track filter on both the Home page (compact) and the Learning Path page so the section nav and guided-route feature stay consistent.
Use a single coherent DataForge data-table-toolkit identity (tables, sorting, searching, pagination, demos) across the Learning Path page, the track filter and the shared chrome.
Do not introduce off-system styling (a one-off bespoke standalone header, inline-styled div rows, a separate page with no shared card grid) or remove sections from the existing Home overview.
state_constraints: desktop_learning verifies the Learning Path page renders through the shared design system: the shared card grid produces at least six h3 step titles, the shared masthead nav with the registered Learning Path nav-link and footer are present, and the on-page track filter (the 'Path tracks' tab row + readout) is present.

desktop_track_data verifies the track filter is a real control: after clicking the Data track tab the visible step cards filter to the Data track and the readout updates to 'Showing 1 of 6 steps · Data', changed from the pre-click 'Showing all 6 steps'.
mobile_learning verifies the Learning Path page and its track filter hold the same design system at 390px without horizontal overflow, clipped cards or overlapping text.

desktop_home verifies the shared section nav lists the Learning Path nav-link and the same track-filter control appears as a compact rail on the Home page, reachable from a page other than the Learning Path page itself, and the existing Home overview is unchanged.
tablet_home verifies the shared chrome and track filter hold across viewports on the Home page too.

change_completion: The Learning Path page exists at docs/learning-path/ and presents at least six grounded, ordered learning steps that link to real docs pages and demos through the shared card grid.
The docs site's own on-page track filter (All / Setup / Build / Connect / Data / Ship tab row plus a live 'Showing N of 6 steps' readout) sits above the six step cards.
Clicking a track tab filters the visible step cards and updates the readout so it matches the cards shown, and the same control appears as a compact rail on the Home page.
design_consistency: The Learning Path page and track filter reuse the shared masthead nav, .card pattern and type scale and are indistinguishable in system from the Home page.
The active track tab stays legible and the step-card grid keeps stable, non-overlapping dimensions; the Learning Path nav-link renders consistently across the Home and Learning Path pages.
regression: The existing Home overview remains intact with its content, shared masthead nav and footer chrome.
No section is removed from the existing pages and no off-system one-off page replaces the design-system layout.
responsive: The Learning Path page, its track filter and the Home overview render at 390px mobile without horizontal overflow or clipped/overlapping cards.
Page, tab-row and card copy remain readable on mobile and tablet.

author_notes: Add the DataForge docs site's own on-page track filter to the guided Learning Path onboarding route so it conforms to the site's existing product design system and shared masthead/section-nav chrome across every page. The native lever is a documentation section-nav/filter: a track-tab row (All / Setup / Build / Connect / Data / Ship) over the six shared step cards with a live 'Showing N of 6 steps · <Track>' readout, surfaced as a compact rail on the Home page too and registered as a 'Learning Path' entry in the shared nav. The reference composes the page from the shared masthead nav and footer chrome and a card grid built on the existing shared .card pattern at docs/learning-path/, fed by six grounded learning steps (linking to Getting Started, Options, Columns, Events, Dynamically-adding-data and the responsive-layout demo). INFRA: identical declared offline build infrastructure is applied across all legs and is NOT part of the task content: the bare demo docs home is rebuilt into a DataForge docs home with a shared masthead <header> nav, a shared feature card grid and a shared <footer>; the docs/demos/ index header is rebranded to the same shared masthead; a docs.css design-system stylesheet is added and its global overflow-x clamp is neutralized so real horizontal overflow is measurable; every rendered section-nav anchor is given a shared nav-link class; and the generic simple-datatables docs are rebranded into the DataForge identity. This infrastructure is identical across reference, baseline and bad. The baseline keeps the correct filter wiring but its track-tab row is a narrow non-wrapping fixed-width row that overflows a 390px viewport, its step-card grid is a non-wrapping fixed-width flex row whose cards overlap and clip, its active track tab is dark-on-dark illegible, and it mounts the track filter only on the Learning Path page (absent from Home). The bad solution adds the same broken layout and Home-absent mounting AND snapshots the count readout at load, so clicking a track tab flips the active-tab class but the grid keeps showing all six cards and the readout stays frozen on 'Showing all 6 steps'.
